significance.root_decision: The conjecture holds: for all coprime q > p > 2, the difference f_{p,q}(n+1) − f_{p,q}(n) is strictly positive for infinitely many n and strictly negative for infinitely many n, where f_{p,q}(n) counts the representations of n as a sum of distinct numbers p^a q^b. Infinitely many increases follow from the authors' Corollary 3 (f is unbounded). The new part is the decreases: if f were eventually nondecreasing, a comparison at roots of unity would force certain twisted products over pure powers to vanish, while the exact product over all roots of unity gives a uniform lower bound; the contradiction needs p > 2 (for p = 2 the authors prove that f is monotone). Lean defines f by the source's literal representation count and proves both infinitely many strict increases and infinitely many strict decreases, with non-vacuity checks.
significance.caveat: The journal version (J. Number Theory, doi 10.1016/j.jnt.2025.07.009) and the one indexed citing paper (H. Liu, Period. Math. Hungar., doi 10.1007/s10998-026-00707-y) could not be read in full; arXiv v3 and the indexed journal preview still call the statement Conjecture 3, and the citing paper's abstract concerns a different question (reviewer's probability that it settles this conjecture: 0.02). The increases are the authors' own Corollary 3; the contribution is the decreases, a few compact paragraphs. Proof, first (same-model) review and Lean are by Claude Opus 5.5; the cross-model review and final check are by GPT-6.2 Sol (two rounds; not routine 0.58, close to the floor of 0.55 root uses for counting).
